The present reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was received from the office of Land Acquisition Collector on an application moved by the petitioners, who have sought enhancement of the monetary award given by the Land Acquisition Collector on the ground that the assessment of the market value of the acquired land was done on the lower side without considering the relevant factors for correctly assessing the market value of the land in question.
The reference was received from the office of LAC (South) on 22.03.1985.

3.

The present reference under Section 18 of the L.A. Act pertains to the award announced by LAC for acquisition of land situated in village Okhla which was acquired for the public purpose of 'Planned Development of Delhi'.

The land in question was acquired by the LAC vide award No.113/198081 dated 20.02.1981 pursuant to preliminary notification under Section 4 of the Act dated 04.04.1964 which was followed up by notification under Section 6 of the Act on 07.12.1966.
CNR No.  DLST01 0006542015 Pratap Singh (Deceased Through LRs) & Ors.

4. The Land Acquisition Collector (in brief LAC) after considering the relevant factors gave its Award No.113/198081 by determining the compensation for the compulsory acquisition @Rs. 4,200/
per bigha.
5. Since the petitioners did not accept the award, they preferred a reference application under Section 18 of the Act, 1894 before the Land Acquisition Collector, Delhi.
The reference filed by the petitioners along with statement under Section 19 of the Act, 1894 has been sent to the Court by the Land Acquisition Collector for answering the same.
6. Reference was forwarded by the LAC with the claims of the ten petitioners.

The petitioners would state that the LAC had assessed the value of the lands at a low rate, unjustly & arbitrarily, without keeping in mind the various parameters for determining the rate of compensation i.e. for assessing the market value.

The said portions of the land were got from government for welfare and use of the applicants through the office of respondent no. 2 (Delhi Simla CNR No.  DLST01 0006542015 Pratap Singh (Deceased Through LRs) & Ors.

Catholic Society Masihgarh, New Delhi).
The respondent no. 2 (Delhi Simla Catholic Society Masihgarh, New Delhi) never cultivated any land and was only an intermediary absentee paper lessee.
The rights of such intermediaries were abolished under the Preamble of Delhi Land Reforms Act 1954.
However, the land in question was within the notified area, committee on the 20 th of July 1954 when the said Act had come into force.
However, soon after the interest of the applicants were protected by the Delhi Urban Area Tenants Relief Act, 1961 which made them not liable for ejectment.

sentences.text: Therefore, the applicants are permenent lesses paying a nominal fixed rent of 50 paise per bight kham and not liable to ejectment.

Thus, the applicants alone are entitled to receive the whole amount along with the enhanced compensation to the exclusion of respondent no. 2 (Delhi Simla Catholic Society Masihgarh, New Delhi).
7.
It is further stated in the petition that the land had been compulsorily acquired and the petitioners did not have any say in the assessment of the compensation payable to the persons interested.
The lands are situated in the urban area of New Delhi which is one of the Nerve Centre of the World.
The lands sites CNR No.  DLST01 0006542015 Pratap Singh (Deceased Through LRs) & Ors.

have immense potential for residential and for commercial purpose.
The land abut the Delhi Mathura road.
There are educational institution and hospital facilities and other facilities near the lands.
The value assessed of the standing fruits and other trees is low and insufficient.
The compensation assessed is not even equal to one yearly yield from the trees.

Consequently,
petitioners have prayed for grant of enhanced compensation in respect of the acquired land alongwith other benefits.
8. It is pertinent to mention here that in the reference petition, Union of India was the respondent no. 1 while Delhi Simla Catholic Society Masihgarh, New Delhi was the respondent no. 2.
One reference petition under Section 30 - 31 of L.A Act had also been filed which was sent to the Court for decision.

In view of the pendency of the reference petition under Section 3031 of the L.A. Act,
vide order dated 20.11.1987, the present reference under Section 18 of the L. A. Act was stayed sine die.

Thereafter, after the disposal of the said reference under Section 3031 of the L.A. Act, an application was moved on behalf of the petitioners under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure,
1908 for revival of the reference petition under Section 18 of the L. A. Act.

29. ISSUE NO.3 : This issue reads as under :
"3.

Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation, as prayed? OPP"
30.
The present petition has been filed by 10 petitioners claiming enhancement of compensation.

However, as discussed hereinabove, one reference under Section 30 - 31 of L.A. Act was CNR No. 
DLST01 0006542015 Pratap Singh (Deceased Through LRs) & Ors.
Vs . Union of India & Anr.
also sent to the Court in relation to the same properties.

As per the award dated 04.06.2014 in LAC No. 42/2011, the petitioner no. 6 Saran Das and petitioner no. 7 Anaro who were IP No. 14 and 16 respectively before the Court in the LAC No. 42/2011, could not prove their claim and therefore,
their claim was dismissed by the Court.
Therefore, in the present case also, they are held not entitled for any enhanced compensation.
31. In view of findings given under issue No.1 & 2, the petitioner no. 1 to 5 and 8 to 10 are found entitled to receive enhanced compensation.

However, it is noteworthy that in the above mentioned reference under Section 30 - 31 L.A. Act vide LAC No. 42/2011, Ld. Judge had held that the petitioners herein are entitled only to 50% of the compensation and therefore, in the present case also, the petitioner no. 1 to 5 and 8 to 10 shall be entitled for 50 % of the enhanced compensation.
The LAC had awarded the compensation @ Rs. 4,200/ per bigha.

In view of the findings recorded hereinabove, the market value of the land on the date of notification u/s 4 is found to be Rs.
29,025/ per bigha.
Thus, the compensation has been enhanced to Rs. 24,825/ per bigha.

As the petitioners no. 1 to 5 and 8 to 10 are entitlted to only CNR No.  DLST01 0006542015 Pratap Singh (Deceased Through LRs) & Ors. Vs. Union of India & Anr.
50 % of the compensation, I hold that they shall be entitled to enhanced compensation @ Rs.
12,412.50/ per bigha.
32.
